text.p: Sonic Environmental Systems Inc said on Friday that it has voluntarily filed Chapter 11 with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J.

Sonic, a designer and marketer of industrial and commercial environmental control products, filed Chapter 11 to merge with Turbotak Technologies Inc, forming a new company called Turbosonic Technologies Inc. The proposal would cancel Sonic's existing shares, the company said.
The Bankruptcy Court set a hearing April 15, 1997 to determine whether the restructuring should be submitted to a vote of Sonic's creditors, the company said.

Under Sonic's restructuring plan, TurboSonic would have 10 million shares of common stock, with Turbotak's present shareholders owning 82 percent of the company and Sonic shareholders 12.7 percent, the company said.
The remainder of the 10 million shares would be issued to Sonic's existing creditors, the company said.
Sonic said the merger would extinguish Turbotak's secured claims of $1,040,000 against Sonic. Turbotak designs, makes and services air pollution control equipment, the company said.
